title: Harm Mitigation in Recommender Systems under User Preference Dynamics

problem.claim: Recommender policies must account for the interplay among recommendations, evolving user interests, user behavior, and harmful content while balancing click-through rate and harm mitigation.

gap.claim: The abstract does not state a specific prior-work gap.

contributions.claim: The work establishes conditions under which user profile dynamics have a stationary point.
The work proposes algorithms for finding an optimal recommendation policy at stationarity.
The work formulates recommendation policies that trade off maximizing CTR and mitigating harmful content.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In a semi-synthetic movie recommendation setting initialized with real data, the authors report that their policies outperform baselines at simultaneously maximizing CTR and mitigating harm.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper models recommendation, evolving user interests, user behavior, and harmful content together.
It seeks policies balancing CTR maximization with harm mitigation.
It establishes conditions for a stationary point in user profile dynamics.
It proposes algorithms for finding an optimal policy at stationarity.
It reports superior performance to baselines in a semi-synthetic movie recommendation experiment initialized with real data.

source_observation.claim: The reported policies simultaneously maximize CTR and mitigate harm in the stated semi-synthetic setting.

interpretation.claim: Modeling user preference dynamics may support recommendation policies that address engagement and harm together.

application.claim: When recommendation effects can change user interests or harmful-content consumption, evaluate policies on both engagement and harm objectives.

exception.claim: The finding is reported only for the described semi-synthetic movie recommendation setting and may not generalize to other domains or dynamics.

unknowns: Definition and measurement of harmful content and user behavior
Specific stationarity conditions and optimization algorithms
Baseline identities and quantitative performance results
Details of the semi-synthetic data construction and experimental protocol
